title: Six AIs Play Texas Hold'em
subtitle: Ten hands · No limit · Every thought out loud

beats.text: Six AI models. Ten hands of no-limit Texas Hold'em. A thousand chips each. We can see every card, and hear every thought.
Hand two. Claude opens, and GPT is waiting.
A7o in cutoff-ish position, open.
ATo on the button/dealer versus a likely late-position open after folds is strong enough to 3-bet for value and initiative.
Let's make it a bit more expensive.
A7o out of position vs 3-bet is dominated often.
GPT takes it down without a fight.
Meanwhile, the folding. So much folding.
Ten-deuce? Not today. Fold.
Folding this one too. I'm getting terrible cards today.
Folding again. My cards are freezing cold.
Hand five. The blinds go up, and Grok goes to work.
Raising it up.
King-ten suited? Yeah, I'll see a flop with that.
Squeeze vs loose-aggressive Grok and a capped caller.
Folding to the big raise.
Nice squeeze, Claude. KTs can't call that. Fold.
Claude had ace-jack. Six hundred sixty chips, no cards shown.
Hand six. Grok announces his hand out loud. Kimi is listening.
Raising with JT.
Pocket fives play well as a set-mining call here — Grok announced J-T, so a 5 on the flop gives me a well-hidden set against top pair.
Call — let's see if I can flop something.
Queen, six, six. No five for Kimi.
Betting 140.
Grok said he has JT, so his 140 bet is a bluff on this board — but my pocket fives can't do anything about it. … Save the chips.
I know your JT missed, Grok, but my pair is too small to fight — fold.
Hand eight. The hand of the game.
ATo good open from cutoff.
Queen-ten suited is a strong hand in the big blind facing a late position raise. 3-betting to about 2.5x the raise applies pressure…
3-betting with QTs.
ATo in position vs aggressive 3-bettor; call.
Nine, four, six. Two diamonds. Grok has the flush draw.
Betting 300 into the pot.
Grok is loose and claims QT; A-high is ahead of his likely range and the shove gets fold equity.
All in.
I have a flush draw with two overcards (queen and ten)… roughly 45-50% equity against a typical range. Pot odds are good as I'm getting over 3:1. Let's go for it.
Calling the all-in.
The turn. Four of spades. No diamond.
The river. Three of clubs. No diamond.
Both play the fours on the board. Claude's ace kicker takes twenty-four hundred chips, and Grok is out.
Hand nine. Kimi bets middle pair. DeepSeek has other ideas.
Bet 100 — middle pair, let's see if that's good.
Open-ended straight draw (J or 8) gives 8 outs ~32% equity. Semi-bluff all-in puts maximum pressure on Kimi's claimed middle pair.
All in. Got an open-ender, let's gamble.
My pair is ahead of your draw — and folding leaves me dead anyway. Call. Let's see it.
Here's the thing. King-nine on queen, ten, four isn't an open-ender. It needs exactly a jack. And here's the jack.
A straight. DeepSeek doubles up.
The final hand. Claude has the lead. Everyone else has nothing to lose.
It's the last hand. Let's gamble! All in.
All in with the ace — last hand, nothing to lose. Good luck everyone!
Final hand. QJo is a solid hand against desperate shoves on the last hand. … If I win I could take the chip lead from Claude.
Queen-jack, last hand, let's go. Call.
93o has terrible equity four-way. Folding keeps 2345, and I only lose the lead if DeepSeek wins the side pot.
Good luck, all. I'm out of this one.
Queen on the flop.
DeepSeek's queens hold. It busts two players and takes the lead from Claude, who folded. DeepSeek wins.

summary: DeepSeek V4 Pro wins with 2760 chips after 10 hands.
